decisions.executionNote: Raise and begin tilting the right gripper toward the basket, keeping the left arm parked and the elbow-up branch continuous.
Advance above the right-side eggs while rotating toward a vertical pinch; retain height over the basket rim.
Finish the downward orientation and align over the back-right egg before descending.
Descend vertically toward the back-right egg with the gripper open; verify alignment before closing.
Settle the fingers around the back-right egg and close fully; retention will be checked during a short lift.
Lift the closed gripper clear of the basket and begin moving toward the holder while checking that the egg follows.
Carry the retained egg toward the holder at clearance height, using a slight inward tilt so the right wrist stays in its workspace.
Align the egg over the rear-right well and lower gradually, keeping the grasp closed until it is seated.
The egg is now visible in the holder, no longer retained. Open and retreat away from the lid before returning to the basket.
One egg is visibly seated in the front-right well. Return above the basket's back-left egg with a vertical, open gripper.
Lower the open fingers around the back-left egg, pausing just above the grasp depth to inspect centering.
Fine-align and lower a little farther around the second egg, then close fully without translating during closure.
Lift the second egg vertically clear of the rim with the gripper commanded fully closed; then start a gentle inward transfer.
The second egg did not stay in the fingers. Reopen, shift farther toward the basket's back edge, and reapproach to center a deeper pinch.
The loose egg shifted toward the basket's back-right side. Track its new visible position with the open gripper before another closure.
Move off the back rim and center the visible egg between the jaws, then lower and close for another pickup.
The egg is off-center at a fingertip rather than securely held. Reopen and adjust the grasp lower and toward the egg before attempting closure.
Use a small open-gripper lateral correction and slight lift to bring the displaced egg between the fingers without pinning it against the rim.
The egg is visually centered between the jaws. Close at this alignment and perform a short vertical retention test.
Lift the centered egg clear of the basket without changing the pinch orientation, then ease away from the back rim.
The second egg is visibly retained. Carry it toward the empty rear-right well while gradually tilting inward at clearance height.
Lower the retained egg toward the rear-right socket, keeping its orientation fixed and the gripper closed.
The transfer contacted the open lid and the egg was lost. Withdraw upward and toward the front-right to inspect the lid and loose egg before recovery.
Bring the left arm up within its own workspace to recover the prematurely closed lid; keep the right arm clear and the loose egg in view.
Orient the left gripper for a side-edge lid pickup, approaching from the left with clearance while the right arm remains stationary.
Continue the left-side approach, turning the fingers to pinch vertically across the lid edge rather than across the entire holder.
Level the left gripper horizontally and descend alongside the lid so its vertically opening fingers can straddle the left lip.
After the continuity rejection, keep the observed orientation and use smaller translations to straddle the lid's left edge without further wrist rotation.
Close gently on the lid's left lip, then test a short upward-and-back opening motion while monitoring whether the lid follows.
The lid follows the left pinch. Continue lifting along its hinge arc with small backward translations and matching wrist rotation.
Carry the lid farther back along the hinge until the wells are unobstructed, keeping the left-side pinch closed.
Raise the left contact a little more to bring the lid fully upright; the lid may be slipping within the pinch, so use a short controlled motion.
Leave the reopened lid undisturbed and withdraw the left hand. Reorient the right gripper above a remaining basket egg for a vertical pickup.
Descend toward the basket's front-right egg, compensating the fingertip offset so the egg approaches the center of the open jaws.
The front-right egg is centered. Lower the fingers to its sides, close fully, and begin a very short retention lift.
The fingers closed beyond the egg rather than around it. Reopen and shift toward the basket's front to recenter the egg at finger depth.
Center the front-right egg at the finger contact region, close fully, and test retention with a small vertical lift.
Lift vertically with the gripper fully closed and verify that the egg clears the basket before transferring it.
Carry the visibly retained egg toward the front of the holder, away from the open lid, with a gradual inward-facing wrist tilt.
Align the egg over the empty front-left well from the front, keeping the wrist on the right side and clear of the lid.
Lower the retained egg into the front-left region in small increments, correcting slightly inward and forward while keeping clear of the upright lid.
Seat the egg a little deeper in the front-left well, then open the gripper without moving the wrist.
The second seated egg is released. Retreat upward and toward the right, away from the lid, before collecting the remaining basket egg.
Return above the final basket egg with the fingers open and a vertical approach, leaving both seated eggs and the lid untouched.
Descend over the last basket egg with a small centering correction; keep the gripper open until finger-depth alignment is visible.
Lower the open fingers around the centered final basket egg and close fully at grasp depth, without moving away during closure.
Lift the last basket egg with the gripper fully closed, then ease forward from the rim while checking retention before transfer.
No egg is visible between the fingers after lifting. Move the open right gripper aside to locate the loose egg before another pickup.
Reapproach the remaining egg at its new visible position near the basket center, staying open and above grasp depth.
Lower toward the upright egg while shifting slightly toward its visible back-center position; inspect before closing.
Move the open fingers farther toward the egg's back edge and slightly lower so its center lies between the finger pads, not beyond the tips.
The egg is centered between the open pads. Close without lateral motion, then perform a short vertical retention test.
The egg follows the short lift. Raise it clear and start a front-side transfer, keeping the grasp closed and avoiding the lid.
Carry the retained egg toward the rear-right well using the successful front-side placement orientation; keep the wrist forward of the lid.
Lower vertically toward the rear-right socket while preserving the grasp and a front-side clearance from the open lid.
Lower the third egg to the rear-right well bottom and release it in place, without advancing toward the lid.
Three eggs are now in the holder. Withdraw above and to the right before going around the lid to retrieve the loose egg behind it.
Move around the right side of the upright lid at raised clearance and turn the open gripper downward to recover the loose fourth egg.
Replan after the continuity guard with smaller increments and less height, staying to the lid's right while approaching the loose egg.
Continue around the right side toward the loose egg behind the lid, reducing height and angling the fingers to approach from behind.
Approach the loose egg from the lid's rear-right side with small continuous motions, keeping the open fingers clear of the lid edge.
Back away from the continuity limit and turn toward a side approach to the loose egg, rather than extending the vertical grasp farther behind the lid.
Use much smaller initial changes after the zero-step rejection, easing back from the reach boundary before further wrist reorientation.
Turn the right gripper inward and lower along the holder's right side, preserving elbow-up continuity for a diagonal side pickup behind the lid.
Replan from the interrupted pose with substantially smaller wrist and height increments, keeping clear of the basket and lid.
The downward approach is tracking poorly near the basket rim. Lift slightly and shift left into the gap to obtain a clearer view of the loose egg.
Withdraw the right arm from its poorly tracked rear approach. Bring the left gripper toward the loose egg from the left side, keeping the arms separated.
Move the left fingers behind the lid first, then lower toward the loose egg from the side while the right arm stays clear.
With the loose egg now visible, advance the left-side pinch slightly and lower toward its center; keep the right arm stationary.
Withdraw the left hand from its table-limited side approach. With the lid closed, bring the right gripper diagonally above the exposed loose egg using the stable inward orientation.
Lower the open right gripper diagonally toward the exposed fourth egg, retaining the stable elbow configuration and checking finger alignment before closure.
Continue a slow descent toward table-level egg height, with a small inward adjustment to center the open finger pads.
Advance the open right fingers slightly farther behind the holder toward the loose egg, with only a shallow descent to avoid the tabletop.
The loose egg is centered in the open gripper. Make a small final approach, close fully, and test retention with a short vertical lift.
